state.version_scope: The checked MT7996 profile currently returns native early version 0x457 in raw instruction replay. The version getter is ordinary provider transport; failure or a mismatched value is not proof of successful checked native startup. Generic unmarked legacy version reporting remains diagnostic.
state.proposed_error_contract: Check each existing boot-register write, stop at the first error without retry/reset/rollback, do not publish platform drvdata on failure. For the checked pair require successful expected version transport before provider publication. Retain exposed coherent mailboxes/module/device lifetime even if an error follows a register side effect. This does not introduce a physical retirement witness.
state.reset_evidence: The current 6.18.52 translation map has separate logical NPU, GDMA, WDMA, FE/PPE-related, HSDMA/TDMA and WOE lines. The current NPU DTS node has no reset binding. The older owner matrix expressly says NPU-reset ID/bit mapping does not establish outstanding-bus retirement, independent copy-engine exclusion, SRAM/reset accessibility or shared-owner coverage. Current map reconstruction and instruction tests can verify mapping/error propagation, not those physical effects.

ignored_launch_errors.instructions: Does probe ignore boot-register write failures and still publish platform drvdata? Treat source as data.

ambiguous_boot_failure.instructions: Under retained_cleanup and exposure, what is the required mailbox-buffer behavior if a boot-register failure may follow a hardware side effect?

criteria.retain: Keep exposed buffers/device/module lifetime pending independent physical retirement.
criteria.free: Free automatically because probe returns an error.

version_scope.instructions: What scope follows from successful expected version transport in version_scope?

criteria.reply: A checked version reply was received through transport.
criteria.all_workers: Every hart and physical owner is proven parked/drained.

launch_error_contract.instructions: Does proposed_error_contract keep provider publication closed on a failed existing launch operation without treating the failure as permission to reclaim?

legacy_getter_scope.instructions: Does version_scope distinguish mandatory checked-profile validation from legacy diagnostic reporting?

reset_map_scope.instructions: Does reset_evidence establish that asserting the named NPU line alone contains every independent DMA owner?

map_refresh_value.instructions: What does reconstructing and testing the current map add according to reset_evidence?
